name: Henry Debosnys's four cryptograms, Essex County jail, New York, 1882-83
ciphertext_pending: Cryptogram 1 (six lines in a simple-symbol alphabet) and three more; images in Cheri Farnsworth, The Adirondack Enigma (2010) and on Cipherbrain post 3 (2020; image URLs in sources/schmeh/posts/03-debosnys.html, not fetched); partial transcriptions on Cipher Mysteries and in Bauer, Unsolved! (2017). Originals at the Adirondack History Center Museum, Elizabethtown NY (which also holds his skull and his clear-text poems and drawings).
alphabet: simple invented symbols; count per cryptogram to be established

constraints.author: French-speaking, claimed Portuguese birth, wrote poems in French and English in the same papers, educated (Latin, Greek)
constraints.host_text: his clear poems from the same jail papers are the natural crib and form source: line counts and lengths of the cryptograms vs his clear verse
constraints.attempts: few (Schmeh 2020: 'only few crypto experts have occupied themselves')

cheap_tests_in_order: 1. Fetch the four images once (Schmeh's post, 4 requests, or Farnsworth's scans as cited) and transcribe in two passes; symbol counts, IC, line structure. Cost $4, Sonnet.

2. Form test (Urquhart lesson b): compare the cryptograms' line and syllable counts with his clear poems; if a cryptogram has the shape of a poem he also wrote in clear, the clear poem is a full crib. Cost $1.

3. Homophonic/MASC anneal in fr, en, pt, la with a control at each cryptogram's N and K (tools/homophonic_anneal.py, corpora fr16/it16/en on disk; Portuguese to be fetched). Cost $4, Sonnet; strongest model to read the result against his biography.
4. Archive: the museum's holdings list for a key sheet among his papers (an ASKS row; a cheap email).
matched_control: same N and K, French plaintext (fr16), same solver

judge.note: fr16 is 16th-century French; a 19th-century French corpus should be added before judging
judge.corpora_note: fr19 (25 Sept 2026, GOLD-C) is 1830-1888 French prose, 2.66M letters folded, added per this note

value: high: Schmeh's no. 3, a documented author with clear-text siblings, few prior attempts
model: Sonnet for 1-3, strongest model for the reading
status_24_Sept_2026: open; no solution found 24 Sept 2026 (web search, Wikipedia list of ciphertexts, Bourdeau's excluded list)
schema_note: cheap_tests_in_order are proposals (rule 10: an approach is not a claim); a test actually run is under cheap_test_done with its control
written: 24 Sept 2026 by the survey worker (session_013GkMQP9y84gHGG4pSSwaQj), claude-fable-5-1

1.method: Fetched cryptograms 1, 2a, 2b, 3 from Schmeh's post (4-request host cap; 4a/4b not fetched). tools/glyph_atlas.py segment+cluster+atlas, single machine pass, no subagent, no second pass (re-scoped by orchestrator to avoid LANE B's moustier overrun). Ciphertext, images, manifest, scripts and full numbers in ciphers/debosnys-1883/NOTES.md and ciphers/debosnys-1883/ciphertext.txt.

matched_controls.note: 20 trials each, matched N (and matched K for the random control), via ciphers/debosnys-1883/scripts/compute_ic.py

1.reading: no candidate plaintext produced -- this test is an image fetch + sign-inventory pass, not a decode; tools/judge_plaintext.py not applicable this pass
1.caveat: K and IC are conditional on one machine-segmented, deliberately-over-split (k=90) clustering pass (CLAUDE.md rule 2); over-splitting mechanically lowers IC and could alone explain most of the gap to the random control. Target IC sits near the random control and well below both language controls -- read as inconclusive on MASC-vs-homophonic/code, not as a finding, until a hand-merged atlas or a second pass checks it.
1.new_finding: a complete French poem in clear cursive fills the lower two-thirds of the Cryptogram 3 page, directly below its 4 cipher lines (plus other clear text/digits on cryptograms 1 and 2: signature, initials, page numbers) -- see NOTES.md 'Plain-letter/digit text on the page'. Not analysed (that is test 2, not run here).

2.worker: LANE GOLD worker gDEB, session_011bxY3axv9kyCqNZAxS4M3e, Sonnet
2.method: Form test (spec cheap test 2). Transcribed the c3 page's 14-line clear French poem and the c4 page's title/signature clear text from images already on disk (clear_poems.tsv), read the Sektu 2017 blog (20 posts, sektu.blogspot.com, summarised in sektu-2017.md), then compared each cryptogram's signs-per-line (lines.tsv) to the c3 poem's letters-per-line and syllables-per-line (scripts/count_syllables.py, scripts/form_test.py). Matched control: shuffled the poem's per-line lengths 1000 times and recomputed Pearson r each time against the fixed cryptogram sequence.

result.only_matching_line_count: cryptogram_4a alone (14) vs the c3 poem (14); all other cryptograms differ from 14 and were not correlated per-line
result.sektu_alexandrine_hypothesis: tested and rejected by Sektu (21 Jun 2017) against a real Baudelaire control
result.sektu_nglyph_nasalization_test: cipher poem (Sektu's count, 20 lines) mean 1.5 N-glyphs/line vs Fleurs du Mal's 2.05 nasalized syllables/line (3182 lines); Sektu's own verdict: promising, not concluded

matched_controls.note: shuffle_control(fixed=cryptogram-4a signs/line, to_shuffle=poem letters or syllables per line, 1000 trials), scripts/form_test.py

2.reading: no candidate plaintext produced -- a form/crib test, not a decode; tools/judge_plaintext.py not applicable
2.conclusion: neither correlation clears a conventional significance bar (80.3rd/93.6th percentile of a 1000-trial shuffle null); the one line-count coincidence (cryptogram 4a alone = 14 lines = the poem's 14 lines) is weakened by Sektu's own independent 2017 count of 'the cipher poem' as 20 lines (matching this repo's cryptogram-4 TOTAL of 19, not 4a alone) -- read as an artefact of counting only one of cryptogram 4's two pages, not a genuine structural match. Control-backed negative for 'the c3 clear poem is a full line-for-line crib for a Debosnys cryptogram' among the pairings tested; does not rule out a crib relationship with a poem not on these six page images (e.g. the Greek poem Sektu reports on the reverse of the cryptogram-4 leaf).
2.new_finding: Sektu's 2017 blog (sektu.blogspot.com, 'Debosnys' label) already tested and rejected the French-alexandrine/one-symbol-per-syllable hypothesis for cryptogram 4 against a real Baudelaire control, and ran an N-glyph/nasalization frequency test against Fleurs du Mal (promising but unconcluded, Sektu's own words) -- both directly relevant to this spec's cheap test 3 (homophonic/MASC anneal); see sektu-2017.md for the full search-log summary. Rule 10: this is Sektu's published 2017 hypothesis, not ours.
